lines: PRESIDENT:  Thank you.  Very good morning to all of you.
We will continue today with the examination of the
last claimant's witness.  We have, I think,
Mr Colombo, who is going to give testimony to the
tribunal.
MR HAUGENEDER:  He's ready and we will ask him to
come in.
MR FRANCESCO COLOMBO
PRESIDENT:  Good morning, Mr Colombo.  Thank you for
coming to this hearing to give testimony.  I will
remind you, if you don't, if you're not aware of the
process.
First, I will ask you to read an affirmation about
your willingness to give to the tribunal truthful
testimony.  Then I will invite counsel for claimant to
first affirm your witness statements and ask you a few
questions in direct examination.  And then we have
scheduled cross-examination for 30 minutes to be
conducted by respondent.  And if claimant needs, he
will ask you questions in redirect.  And then the
tribunal may ask you questions as well.
You will be provided with documents on the screen
and you should have in front of you your witness
statement.
A  Yes.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.  For the record, will you please
read, state your name and read aloud the affirmation.
A  I Francesco Colombo, do solemnly, sincerely, and truly
declare and affirm that the evidence I shall give
shall be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but
the truth.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.
Examination-in-chief by MR HAUGENEDER
MR HAUGENEDER:  Good morning.
A  Good morning.
Q  Mr Colombo.  You have submitted a witness statement in
this arbitration, which you have in front of you.  Can
you confirm the correctness of that witness statement?
A  I do confirm.
Q  Do you wish to amend or correct anything in that
statement?
A  No, nothing to be changed.
Q  Mr Colombo, your witness statement deals with hedging.
Could you please explain to us, what is a hedge?  What
is the purpose of a hedge?
A  So in general terms, a hedge is a contract by which
a company, any company, can lock in the margin between
the purchase and the sales leg of a specific
transaction, in case either leg has a different price
nature from the other.  So the hedge helps in
eliminating this difference and locking in the margin
of the transaction.
Q  What is the hedging policy of PPD?
A  So the hedging policy of PPD is to hedge, therefore
eliminate any kind of difference between the two legs
in purchase and sale, immediately, right after the
conclusion of the transaction.
Q  So do you try to hedge all transactions, if possible?
A  Absolutely.  So when company I work for, PPD Global,
is given the task to hedge from PPD, we always hedge
or try to hedge 100 per cent of the quantity within
the contract for the whole duration of the contract.
Q  Your witness statement then deals with lot 1 of the
HEP contracts concluded in 2021.  Have you attempted
to hedge that contract as well?
A  Yes, we did try.  We first requested indications to
counterparties in order to hedge those contracts,
especially the lot 1, before the lot 1 was concluded.
And then once lot 1 was concluded and we received the
order from PPD, we tried to hedge as much as we could.
However, this ended up with being only 19 per cent
of the whole quantity of the contract, so about
80 per cent was left unhedged.
Q  And what was the reason you couldn't hedge the
remaining 80 per cent?
A  The reason was the lack of credit opening or
availability from our pool of counterparties, because
of the market scenario which was happening during
Q4 2021, which was quite unprecedented compared to the
past scenarios we have seen.
Q  And could you explain that market environment a bit,
please?
A  So basically, our counterparties give us the right or
the price to hedge depending on their credit risk
towards PPD, in this case, PPD Global.
Usually we always been successful in hedging
because the market scenario and prices were quite
stable.  So our means were considered enough for the
counterparty to enter into a transaction.
However, the increase in prices, and not only in
prices but also in price volatility, so swings up and
down, made our counterparties way more cautious.  So
we were requested to provide additional collaterals,
bank guarantees, cash, which at that time PPD couldn't
give.  And therefore we were, let's say, refused to
hedge the whole quantity, the entire quantity of the
lot 1.
Q  Other than that transaction, has it ever happened to
you that you were unable to hedge a transaction?
A  No, it never happened.
Q  Since when are you with PPD?
A  I work for PPD since 2017.  The company is operative
since 2018.  But the first and the real tough moment
in terms of hedging happened in Q4 2021, when the
price scenario became unbearable for many.
Q  Now, you said that 80 per cent of that transaction
were unhedged.  Can you explain why PPD would suffer
a damage when you were unable to hedge?
A  So lot 1 spans from for the second half of 2022.  So
this contract was concluded in December 2021 and the
delivery of the good, which is natural gas, happens,
would happen from the 1st -- sorry, 1st of July till
the end of December 2022.
Now, the price of the contract was a fixed price,
56 euro per megawatt hour, which was the market level
at that time.
However, without the hedge, the 80 per cent of the
quantity could be in loss for PPD if the market price
realised during the delivery of the contract was
higher, would be higher than 56, and PPD had to buy
gas at those prices.
So it was not sure that the contract would be in
a loss.  However, it was at a high risk due to the
scenario of increase in prices which was verifying
in Q4.
Q  And what was then the actual --
A  What happened is that prices were even higher, so the
company was at a loss.
Q  So can you give us -- can you explain to us what were
these prices roughly at the time PPD had to procure
gas?
A  They were even double than the fixed price of the
contract.
Q  You are an experienced trader.  What is your view
of -- what was the reason of the market environment
that you described in Q4 2021?
A  Let's say we came from the Covid crisis, so prices
were at their lowest ever in 2020.  Then when the
economy picked up at the end of 2020 and 2021, prices
went back to normal levels.  "Normal levels" means
historically normal levels.
However, certain rumours of storages not being
filled by Gazprom in Europe, about smaller volumes
being sold by Gazprom again in their electronic sales
platforms, came up in the second half of 2021, and
this generated several, let's say, small or big price
shocks, which became very evident in Q4.
Basically, after every headlines about gas being
less available during the winter of 2021, 2022, the
prices went up quite consistently.
Q  By how much?
A  Roughly by even 10, 15 per cent per day, which is not,
let's say, a usual percentage in terms of volatility
compared to what we observe, let's say, before the
crisis.
MR HAUGENEDER:  Thank you very much, Mr Colombo.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.
Cross-examination by MS SOLDATENKOVA
MS SOLDATENKOVA:  Good morning, Mr Colombo.
A  Good morning.
Q  My name is Natalia Soldatenkova.  I'm counsel for
Gazprom Export, respondent in the present case.
I will ask you a series of brief questions
concerning your witness statement.
As we have limited time, please, I would be very
grateful if you could answer specifically the question
asked, and I apologise in advance if I ever have to
interrupt you.
When I will ask you to refer to a document,
I will -- this document will be shown on the screen,
and I will also provide you with a printed copy of the
document.
Mr Colombo, you confirmed that you prepared your
witness statement yourself.  Did the lawyers assist
you in this task?
A  I prepared this myself.
Q  Did the lawyers suggest any changes?
A  No, they didn't.
Q  Did they ask you to address any particular facts and
omit some other facts from the witness statement?
A  No.  They didn't.
Q  Thank you.
Mr Colombo, you are CEO of PPD Global SA, right?
A  Correct.  That's correct.
Q  And this is a Swiss entity owned by Mr Pavao Vujnovac,
right?
A  It's a Swiss entity now owned by Mr Pavao Vujnovac,
yes.
Q  And PPD Global SA used to be a subsidiary of claimant,
Prvo plinarsko drustvo, right?
A  Correct.
Q  It was a 100 per cent subsidiary of claimant up to
spring 2023, right?
A  Yes.
Q  And at that moment, the shareholding of PPD was
reduced to 1 per cent?
A  The equity was increased by the IPO.  So the share of
the claimant diluted to 1 per cent.
Q  Thank you.  And you've been an employee of PPD Global
SA for eight years now, right?
A  Since the foundation.
Q  So this is half of your total working experience,
right, quite a long time?
A  More or less, yes.
Q  And you've been employed at PPD Global SA both before
and after that restructuring?
A  That's correct.
Q  Did a lot change in terms of organisation, how the
company functions following the restructuring?
A  No, in operational terms, not that much.  In, let's
say, governance terms, the board has changed.  So when
the restructuring happened, then also the board has
changed.
Q  And you also became the CEO following the
restructuring?
A  Correct, that's correct.
Q  And you are also simultaneously a member of the board
of PPD Italia, right?
A  Yes.  This company is now named ENNA Next Italia
because of the rebranding, but it still belongs to the
group.
Q  At paragraph 2 of your witness statement, you
mentioned that you have been involved in assisting
claimant in arranging hedging transactions.  Do you
still continue to provide those services to claimant?
A  Sorry, that's paragraph number 2?
Q  Paragraph number 2.
A  Can you repeat the question again?  Sorry.
Q  Can you please have a look at the third sentence where
you mentioned that you have been involved -- the
second sentence, third line:
"I have been involved in assisting Prvo plinarsko
drustvo ... in arranging hedging transactions to
balance the risk of PPD's supply and delivery
agreements."
A  Yes, that is --
Q  You continue to provide those services?
A  We keep on doing these services to PPD.
Q  And you mentioned that when PPD Global would assist
PPD with hedge, it would enter into two back-to-back
hedging transactions, right?  So one with the hedging
partner and one with PPD?
A  That's correct.
Q  Is there any framework agreement in place between PPD
and PPD Global pursuant to which those hedging
transactions are concluded?
A  Yes.  There are financial and physical framework
agreements, which are industry standards and in line
with the agreements we have with the other
counterparties, according to which we can enter into
those transactions with PPD.
Q  And you also mentioned that those hedging transactions
are entered into with non-PPD entities.
Are any of the hedging transactions on behalf of
PPD entered into with other PPD subsidiaries, as the
companies of the group?
A  Currently, PPD Global developed the portfolio of,
let's say, other counterparties.  So we provide
similar, not exactly the same, services to other
counterparties, to other entities.
However, back in 2020, 2021, the aim of PPD Global
was mostly the market -- to provide the market access
to PPD.  So back then there were like very few other
counterparties, contrary to now.
Q  Thank you, Mr Colombo.
In paragraph 9, if we could please show it on the
screen, you mentioned that PPD Global -- yes, that
would be the very first sentence where you describe
how hedging is usually arranged.  And you mentioned
here that:
"... PPD Global is usually contacted by PPD at two
stages of the transaction."
So PPD first contacts PPD Global during
contractual negotiations to request pricing
information, correct?
A  That's correct.  And we usually give a first
assessment whether this transaction is feasible, in
which terms of timeline and what level of price is
achievable, by asking to several, as many as possible
counterparties the same request.
Q  And your role also includes overseeing the operations
of the company, I mean overall operations of PPD
Global, right?
A  Yes.  This was even more true back then than now.
Q  And PPD Global has subsidiaries in Bosnia and
Herzegovina in Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Romania and
Croatia.  Right?
A  Yes, in Italy that's PPD Italia, which is not part of
PPD Global anymore.
Q  Thank you.  And those --
A  So, I'm sorry to interrupt.  The Romanian one has just
been dissolved, if I'm not wrong.
Q  Thank you for confirming.  And those are former
subsidiaries of PPD, claimant in this proceeding,
right?
A  Those companies have been acquired by PPD Global from
PPD.
Q  In 2024, correct?
A  That's correct.
Q  At paragraph 6 of your witness statement, you mention
that within the group of companies -- we could go to
the paragraph to assist.  That is the second sentence.
So you are saying here that:
"Within the group of companies, the role of
PPD Global is to balance the group's portfolio through
negotiating physical and financial hedging
transactions."
Right?
A  That's correct.  Yes.
Q  So PPD regularly enters into contracts with PPD Global
and its subsidiaries; it is correct?
A  Yes, this is the nature of the business.  This was the
nature of the business of PPD Global, and the reason
why it was established in the first place.
Q  Thank you.  It is a normal practice in the gas
industry, isn't it, to link agreements for the supply
of gas to industry-wide index prices?
A  Yes, it is quite a common practice, but --
Q  And basically -- apologies.  Basically, this is
a fluctuation of this index that is being hedged by
PPD Global?
A  Yes.  Especially, I mean, we as PPD Global enter into
the game when the other leg of the contract is not on
a floating index.  So when either the purchase or the
sale leg are on a fixed price, besides the other leg
is on a floating price, that's when you need the
hedge.
Q  Thank you.  And at the end of 2021, you mentioned this
in your witness statement, paragraph 17, many
participants were trading speculatively.  That is,
without the underlying contract for physical delivery.
Correct?
A  Can I just see the paragraph?
Q  That would be sentence starting with:
"There was also a general concern..."
And then you mentioned that:
"... many participants were treating
speculatively..."
A  I mean, for sure, companies having different mandates
than PPD Global and having better access to cash
resources, because back then cash was very crucial to
be active on the market, speculated, because when
there is volatility, speculation may bring high
profits.
What I mean in this paragraph is that the lack of
credit that we receive from our counterparties was
also due to the fact that they were -- they wanted to
be sure or they couldn't be sure that we were not
speculating, because of course, speculating at that
time was very appealing.  Which doesn't mean that
everyone was speculating, but the counterparties we
had, which were mostly banks and traders, so very
careful on the risk side, they didn't want to enter
into transactions without being 100 per cent sure that
those transactions were meant to hedge.  And sometimes
there was just a level of trust to be used because it
was not possible to show anything more.
Q  So the actions of those other market participants
effectively contributed to the market volatility,
right?  And to availability of hedging transactions?
A  I think the market volatility was due to the enormous
sequence of headlines, which were coming up every day,
and which is similar to what we are seeing these days,
for other reasons.
So this very frequent headlines generated market
volatility and price spikes especially.  And there was
also a clear lack of availability of volumes.  So
a physical constraint coming up in summer -- in,
sorry, winter '21.
And when this happens, probably there is
a tendency for some companies to try to speculate,
which is a concern that many have.
I'm not saying this was our behaviour, and
I cannot say if this was the behaviour of
somebody else.
Q  But this speculative trading did give concerns to
banks, yes?  So that was one of the reasons why the
banks were generally concerned during that period?
A  The main concern of the banks towards PPD were that
the hedge that PPD would enter eventually into would
end up being on a very negative result.
So the fixed price against the floating price
would mean a huge payment from PPD to -- from
PPD Global, sorry, to the counterparty, and PPD Global
not having the cash availability to satisfy those
payment requests.  And this was their main concern.
And what I say, what I mean by saying not having
enough cash, it also means that we had to use cash for
other reasons, because we were seeing defaults from
our counterparties.
Q  Thank you, Mr Colombo.
In paragraph 24 of your witness statement, you
explain -- I will just give you some time to open
that.
You explained that PPD took steps to hedge lot 2
and lot 3 at the same time as lot 1, correct?  That
was in December 2021.
A  Yes, correct, that was at the beginning of
December 2021.
Q  Nevertheless, as you explained, due to higher market
prices during that period, the delivery period of
lot 1 compared to lot 2 and lot 3, it was more
difficult to hedge it.  You confirm the statement,
right?
A  Yes, I confirm.
Q  And today during your direct examination, you
confirmed that you try to hedge 100 per cent of the
quantity under the contracts, that this is a general
rule, the general practice of PPD, right?
A  Yes.  We always try to hedge the whole quantity that
is given and confirmed to us by PPD.
Q  You also confirmed that it never happened to you that
you were unable to hedge the transaction since you
start in the company in 2017, right?
A  Correct.  It was never a problem.
Q  Can I please take you also to paragraph 11 at page 4
of your witness statement?
Here you also specifically refer to the policy
with respect to contracts with HEP, which had fixed
price, and you say that:
"Where the contract is for deliveries at a fixed
price, like the HEP Contract, we aim to hedge the full
amount under the contract."
Do you confirm this?
A  Yes, I do confirm that we aim always to hedge the full
amount, so the full quantity for the full duration
under the contract.
Q  But PPD did not hedge all contracts even before 2021,
right, on all occasions?  For example, it did not
hedge 100 per cent of its contracts in 2019 and 2022,
right?
A  Can you show me the contracts and some evidence,
please?
Q  Yes.  We would invite you to have -- if you could open
tab {G2.6-103}.  That would not be the contract, but
that would be --
DR REINER:  Could you please give the exhibit number.
MS SOLDATENKOVA:  That would be a table in FIDEM-5, which
analyses the information on the hedging transactions
provided by Mr Way, expert for the claimant.
DR REINER:  Thank you.
MS SOLDATENKOVA:  We will see on the screen the source.
This is a wrong tab I think we see on the screen.
And if you could go to page 103, right, table 11.
Can you please zoom it in.
So there were in total six contracts from 2020 --
2019, which weren't hedged.
A  If I'm not wrong, I mean these dates quite back in
time, but most of those contracts, maybe only number 5
in this table, but all the others should be on
a flexible terms.
So contrary to the lot 1 of HEP contract, those
other transactions concluded with HEP had certain
flexibility in it.  With flexibility, I mean HEP had
the right to decide on daily basis to take from zero
up to 100 per cent of the quantity on their own will.
And the nature of such agreements cannot be hedged
financially in the way that PPD Global hedges
financially the, let's say, other transactions.
So if I'm not wrong back then, PPD decided to
hedge or protect the risk of deliveries under those
contracts by other means.  And with other means,
I refer to assets owned by PPD, such as storages,
where PPD had already gas in storage and via those
assets could deliver on daily basis the quantities
requested by HEP in this case.
So this is why -- we didn't hedge financially so
there is no record of a matching transaction, yes, but
there were other means that PPD used to hedge the risk
under those contracts.
Q  And in your witness statement, paragraph 11, which we
have seen, you mentioned that you hedge all contracts,
all deliveries at fixed price, right?  And those six
contracts were also at fixed price, weren't they?
A  Those contracts were at fixed price, but not at fixed
quantity.  That is the difference behind, I mean
between what we are aiming to hedge and what we don't
hedge, or what PPD doesn't hedge.
So the difference between these contracts and the
lot 1 is the flexibility in terms of volumes.
Q  But you did not distinguish with this respect, with
respect to different kinds of contracts at
paragraph 11, right, of your witness statement?
A  No, it's not explicitly written in paragraph 11.
Q  Thank you.  And just to confirm, you were already at
PPD Global at the time, yes?  So from 2019 to 2020,
this period is when you were already at the company?
A  I started in PPD Global in 2017, so I was there.
Q  Thank you.  If I could go, please, to paragraph 15 of
your witness statement.  You say in the beginning that
you agree with Ms Measic that the market situation in
2021 and 2022 affected PPD Global's attempts to agree
hedging transactions on behalf of PPD, right?
A  Yes, correct.
Q  And then as you describe the situation in
paragraph 19.3, you mention that the situation
essentially became worse in the beginning of 2022,
because counterparties also began to ask for
additional security in the form of bank guarantees
because of the high prices in the market.  Right?
A  Yes.  Basically, the situation dragged on, started in
Q4 2021 and continued in 2022.  What we see, what we
saw becoming worse and worse was the increase of
prices which deteriorated our availability, our cash
availability and access to resources.  Yes.
Q  But in April 2022, I understand, PPD overhedged one
HEP contract, didn't it?
A  We did hedge in 2022 other contracts, among them some
HEP contracts, yes.
Q  Can we please go to the third witness statement by
Ms Measic, to paragraph 36.  I am not sure if you have
it before you, so I can bring you the printed copy.
A  Yes, please.
Q  If that would help.
Can we please open it also on the screen?  That
would be the third witness statement by Ms Measic.
That would be {C1.3}.
And if we could go, please, to paragraph 36.
So here Ms Measic describes that in April 2022 PPD
overhedged one HEP contract, right?
A  Yes.
Q  So while you're saying in your witness statement that
there was no demand on the market to hedge, PPD Global
was able to find demand to overhedge this particular
contract, right?
A  What I say in the statement is that it was difficult
to find counterparties, let's call it appetite from
our counterparties, to enter into transactions.  And
we had to negotiate and explain very carefully the
reason why we were asking for certain transactions.
That overhedge happened because of a mistake.
So PPD Global received the quantity higher and
overhedged this, but -- received a communication of
a quantity higher and overhedged.  And of course we
were experiencing difficult times asking to
counterparties their availability.  It doesn't mean
counterparties always said no.  It means that
counterparties needed more time to evaluate the
feasibility and requested some comfort from us.
Q  And apparently with this particular contract, there
was no problem with appetite, right?  With the one
which was overhedged?
A  In that contract, we managed to hedge even more than
the full quantity of the contract, that's correct.
Q  And this lot 1, after a lot of time passed, you
stopped looking for the hedging opportunities, right?
You mentioned this in your witness statement.
A  We stopped.  However, we had, as said, limited
availability from counterparties, which was changing
week by week according to the market scenario.  And as
we had other requests from PPD at even higher prices,
we concentrated our resources on the new contracts.
Q  And you did not mention this one particular overhedged
contract in your first witness statement, did you?
A  I didn't, no.
MS SOLDATENKOVA:  Thank you, Mr Colombo.
I don't have any further questions for the
witness.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.
I think claimant does not have any question in
redirect, do you?
MR HAUGENEDER:  We do.
PRESIDENT:  Oh, you do?  Sorry.
Re-examination by MR HAUGENEDER
MR HAUGENEDER:  I have only a short question for
clarification.
I think you said it, but I want to be sure that
this came across.  You mentioned flexible contracts
that were shown on the screen.  Just to be sure,
between which parties were those contracts and where
was the flexibility?
A  So the contracts were between PPD and HEP, and the
flexibility was in terms of the demand that HEP could
request to PPD on daily basis.  So probably HEP for
his own needs has -- could have zero demand one day
and 100 per cent demand the other day.  And this was
entirely upon PPD and not upon PPD Global to satisfy
the need of HEP.
Q  And you said such transactions cannot be hedged by
financial hedges.  Could you just explain why briefly?
A  Because the type of financial transactions PPD Global
does are fixed in terms of price, so we exchange
a fixed price for a floating price basically, are
fixed in terms of time, tenure, duration of the
contract and quantity.  So we don't have the
possibility to arrange flexibility in terms of
quantity.  This is done by PPD by other means, usually
assets, such as storages or pipelines, where they can
handle the volumes.
Q  And when you say, you mentioned storage, how do you
control the risk of such transactions by using
storage?
A  PPD has a certain quantity, amount of volume in gas,
of gas, in storage, and uses this quantity to provide
the flexibility his own customer request by, as said,
using the fact -- using the storage as a flexible
asset, so a flexible source of gas.
MR HAUGENEDER:  Thank you.  We have no further questions.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.
No further questions.  Thank you very much,
Mr Colombo.  You have completed your testimony to the
tribunal and you are free to stay here or to go.
Thank you very much.
A  Thank you.  Bye.
(Witness released)
PRESIDENT:  Let's take a five-minute break.
Our next witness is Mr Dmitry Averkin.
MR HAUGENEDER:  Madam President, could we maybe have
a 15-minute break just to organise ourselves better?
PRESIDENT:  Absolutely.
Then let's take a 15-minute break.  Thank you.
We will resume at 25 after the hour.
(Short break)
PRESIDENT:  Counsel for respondent, we are back on
record.  Maybe you would like to bring your
witness in.
And we understand there will be an interpreter,
and the parties have agreed on the interpreter's
qualification and name; this has been agreed in
advance.
MR PAVEL EZHOV (Interpreter)
MR TALANOV:  So, dear members of the tribunal, that is
the interpreter, Mr Pavel Ezhov, and I think he's
ready to make the declaration as agreed.
PRESIDENT:  Good morning to you, sir.
INTERPRETER:  Good morning.
PRESIDENT:  You should have a declaration form in front
of you?
INTERPRETER:  I do have it here.
PRESIDENT:  Can you read it to the tribunal?
INTERPRETER:  Yes.
I, Pavel Ezhov, sincerely and truly declare and
affirm that I will faithfully, accurately and
impartially translate and/or interpret all statements,
documents and communications.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you, sir.
MR DMITRY AVERKIN
PRESIDENT:  Thank you, sir.
INTERPRETER:  Good morning.
PRESIDENT:  Good morning, Mr Averkin.
WITNESS:  Good morning.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you for coming to give testimony in
this case.
The members of the tribunal will hear your
testimony in the following way.  First, I will ask you
to read to the tribunal an affirmation of the
truthfulness of your testimony.  You should have in

WITNESS:  Indeed.
PRESIDENT:  Then I will invite counsel for respondent to
have you affirm your witness statement and ask you

then you will be questioned by the claimant and if

WITNESS:  Clear.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you very much, sir.
So, please state your name and read aloud to the
record the statement in front of you.
WITNESS:  I, Dmitry Averkin, sincerely and truly declare
and affirm that the evidence I shall give shall be the
truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you for testifying in english.  At any
moment, if you need a translation one way or another,
from English to Russian, you have an interpreter next
to you and we will take the time it needs for you to
make sure you're comfortable either way, with the
questions or with the way you want to address the
questions.
WITNESS:  If it would be necessary to be more precise,
I will use the interpreter.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you, sir.
